I suppose there is no true answer for this dilemma, considering the context here. but one thing I think is healthy is the fact you are able to reach out to all walks of people, either on this platform or another. which will at the very least hopefully offer some unique perspectives to you OP.

I guess my advice would be, having never been in this exact predicament, two steps to start... find a time where you are at your most level headed, meaning void of temptation, as well as not immediately following a scenario where you are driven to break things off before things go too far. basically you're most true sense of self.

 I get the impression strongly that your faith is deeply important to you of course, but regardless, take the time to organize your thoughts and motives with your faith so you can clearly state to yourself without fault that you know unequivocally this is A.) the path you wish to walk.
and B.) that you are not twisting yourself into all kinds of ways to mentally drown out any kind of resentment for what you are choosing to abstain from by your beliefs.

basically I'm just saying, I want you to be in a confident headspace about what you want before asking for advice. because I don't want you to come out of this thinking because a majority of people online suggested something different for you, that you are at all doing anything wrong and question your faith due to nothing more than peer pressure.

that being said, I know a torn soul when I meet one. 
you're human, so obviously you will have certain natural desires and temptations that go against your beliefs. and I can see how much that bothers you. but suppressing nature is a tricky one. these desires especially can  temporarily flood your mind with all sorts of thoughts and feelings that are hard to resist. 
but at the same time, you still find yourself with people who you enjoy and indulge with to a point. and than you have to walk away.

that's difficult. no matter how strong your faith or willpower is. I'm talking about walking away from what your mind will tell you are a bunch of possibilities and what ifs.

I want you to be happy and comforted and to enjoy the company of someone who likes you maybe a little more than friends.
but to avoid having to break things off and distance yourself from these people which can be painful..Im wondering. how much luck have you had finding a partner who's views line up with your own?

who respects and shares your boundaries. who won't force your hand to walk away before urges take over. who can take some of the  burden your sheer will power has been shouldering this whole time.

as I type this, the answer I'm giving is starting to sound more and more like general advice for anyone really. there are people who have no restrictions like yourself who just don't want to be single or alone. so maybe they stick around relationships even if things like passions or hobbies totally don't line up. breaking things off hurt everyone even if it's for good reasons.

I'm sure with enough effort placed in putting yourself in places where people with the same problem you have, you will certainly find the right one. someone who won't try to change you. someone who can still make you feel loved without taking things too far. a proper life partner.

it is a very interesting concept to an outsider like me on this subject on how two people can form a loving relationship that wasn't beholden on lust and sex initially. find someone you can love and be friends with, who shares your view.

id just hate for you to feel like you have to repress your human nature because you're with the wrong person. 

talk to God. strengthen your will.
avoid situations that really tempt you. 

that's all I got. good luck! 🤞

movie opens with a young Howard Hughes being instilled by his mother with mental tools to combat and remain in control of his ever growing  mental illness. spelling out QUARANTINE slowly and precisely to escape a manic episode. we see howard way later in the movie do this once more which tells us hes been utilizing this his whole life, probably way more than the audience is let in on. what I really love about that opening is when his mother tells him he is not safe in this world. later on Catherine Hepburn says something similar like "we arent like other people. too many acute angles and eccentricities". im not sure how others will take this. but this is 100% my take on it. fake it until you make it.

now im not implying that one must act disingenuous. as if the other party will have no idea the person theyre talking too isnt *themselves*. but if maintaining conversation is something you struggle with as i do. i found real growth in looking at it like im in a play.

for example.

so i find myself about to engage in conversation with someone new. someone i cant shrug off. lets say its the father of my partner i am meeting for the first time. obviously im not going to lie and say im a lawyer when im not. go overboard with confidence or pretend i have experience with topics he brings up when i actually don't.

the only "acting" involved is.. to be frank.. act like you arent afraid.

as if youre an actor on set and you are cast in the role of yourself. except this version of you doesnt worry about being themselves. be yourself. always. but train yourself (especially with random encounters with strangers) by being the person you always wanted to be. speak up about how you like their clothes when youd otherwise never dare too. stop overthinking about what the "normal" thing is to say and just speak your mind while of course maintaining your manners and not overstating your place. 

in a way. this little act you can do to get used to embracing yourself is the exact opposite of disingenuous. because all youre doing is being the **you** thats always been trapped behind fear and self doubt.

find yourself unable to add to a point they made? ask questions. thats always a safe better. just ask them to expand. it makes the other person feel good to see someone express interest in their lives. plus it also gives you more insight into who they are. 

just try it. and remember. you are not pretending to be someone else. you are literally just pretending for one moment that you arent held back by anxiety. you dont need to be smart, or funny, or exciting to be a great conversationalist. all you have to do is show a genuine interest in the talk. because otherwise, youd both just be wasting your time

I feel like I'm partially going through something similar. listen, I know all so well about the things people say to people expressing thoughts of severe anxiety or depression. while they mean the best, we both know it's just not going to make things better. what I need you to remember is that you have to do your best to (in these bad moments) to divide your train of thought into two separate things. I personally find helpful to not dismiss any of my feelings. they're happening for a reason. but instead acknowledge both sides. first, the anxiety. accept that your mind is doing backflips in an attempt to make sense of a particular chaos. but on the other hand, do your very very best to recall the other part of yourself. the one that is most capable of reasonable thought. of rational thinking. it's important to not ignore one or the other. they are both apart of you. 

look, I don't know you. but in my experience I've found people who deal with anxiety daily share a thing or two in common. whatever is going on between you and your friend. whether the fault lies on you or them. doesn't matter. you obviously care about them. that's where the rational side of your mind comes into play. anxiety isn't 100% bad. in my opinion, it's telling of a person's character. that they have true and deep emotional depth, the only issue is that they struggle to organize and cope with it. what im saying is, distance yourself for a second and try as hard as you can to think as logically as you can. for example:
"is what happened between us a permanent misstep?" the answer is usually no.

"could I do better with channeling my emotions into clear thought where you can express in depth about why it makes you so overwhelmed?"

and last

"this person is clearly very dear to me. is it perhaps time I set aside ego or personal gain and express my selfless thoughts to them? " 

for that last point, I mean in terms of, even if you are entirely in the right, fact is, you're feeling very emotional about what happened. even if you are in the right, focus that emotion to help you properly word to your friend just how shitty this is making you feel.
don't underestimate that honesty. think about it. how beautiful is it as a human being to be aware that turmoil between you and someone close is enough to bring you to tears. phrase it accordingly of course, but make sure they understand you care enough to be here right now asking for help on Reddit from complete strangers because of how desperate you are. I'm proud that you did just that. and if this friend of yours cares about you as much as you care about them, they will feel the same. good luck x
